title: model loading breadcrumbs - weights download & sharding
content:
Quick scratchpad of things tried / notes while debugging model load failures (weights download / checkpoint format / sharding). Mostly for myself, leaving breadcrumbs for whoever picks this up.

Symptom summary:
- Several customers saw model-serving instances fail to initialize during warmup. Failures happen ~10-30% of starts, non-deterministic.
- Error observed: 'RuntimeError: Unexpected EOF while reading checkpoint' or 'ValueError: incompatible tensor shape for key model.layers.3.weight' depending on run.
- When retrying, sometimes load succeeds. Suspected issues: partial download, corrupt shard, inconsistent checkpoint format (legacy single-file vs sharded), or fsspec/S3 flakiness.

Commands I ran (rerunable):
- s3 ls "s3://redwood-models/llama-x/checkpoint-2026-02-20/"
  -> confirmed 8 shard files: checkpoint-00008-of-00008.pt etc
- md5sum on local downloaded shard: md5sum checkpoint-00001-of-00008.pt
  -> matches recorded manifest (manifest.md5 included in bucket)
- curl -I on presigned URL for a shard: curl -I "<presigned-url>"
  -> sometimes returned 200, sometimes truncated response (content-length smaller than expected) when failures observed
- python quick-check script: attempt to stream first 1MB and verify header bytes using fsspec:
  import fsspec, io
  fs = fsspec.filesystem('s3')
  with fs.open(path, 'rb') as f:
      header = f.read(64)
      print(header[:16])
  -> on failure hosts, f.read returned less bytes than expected (no exception)

Typical error snippets from logs:
- "RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading file"
- "UnpicklingError: could not find MARK"
- "ValueError: storage has wrong size for tensor model.embeddings.weight"
- S3 request id: tx-0a1b2c3d4e5f - 403/200 flip shown in gateway logs at same timestamp

Hypotheses / notes:
1) Partial/corrupt downloads due to intermittent S3 network issues or gateway proxies that close connections early. Evidence: truncated content-length, occasional 200 with fewer bytes.
2) Checkpoint version mismatch: newer training pipeline now writes 'safetensors' META but runtime sometimes tries to load as torch .pt (or vice versa). We saw a case where file suffix .pt but header indicated safetensors -> loader mismatches produce weird unpickle errors.
3) Shard ordering / missing shard: if one shard missing or zero-length, torch.load can raise EOF. Manifests typically include shard list but our runtime skips manifest validation on cold start to save latency.
4) Atomic upload issue from training: training job uploads shards in parallel and writes 'completed' marker only after all parts uploaded, but if marker write fails we may see partially present prefix. Need to verify uploader logic.

Repro steps I used locally:
- simulate partial shard: dd if=/dev/zero of=shard.pt bs=1 count=0 seek=1000000 to create zero padded file -> load -> get EOF as expected.
- simulate truncated HTTP by using nc/HTTP server that closes connection mid-stream. Torch load fails similarly.

Quick patch ideas (short term):
- Validate downloads before sleep/warmup: check content-length vs manifest, check MD5/sha256. If mismatch, retry N times.
- Prefer ranged reads and verify header bytes (safetensors vs torch) before full download, fail-fast if header indicates mismatch.
- Add manifest check step in startup: require manifest+completed marker; if missing, backoff and failover to fallback model.
- Change load path to stream-verify: download into tmp file then fs.atomic_rename -> ensures no half-present files. (But we might not control S3 uploads from training side.)

Long-term fixes:
- Coordinate with training team to guarantee atomicity: write marker only after multipart upload completes + manifest with checksums. Add server-side MD5 in metadata.
- Switch to safetensors for all new checkpoints to avoid pickle/unpickle vector issues; ensure runtime picks loader by header not extension.

Notes on libraries / versions that matter:
- fsspec==2024.12.0 used in runtime; earlier hosts used 2024.8 and behaved slightly differently for connection reuse. Consider pinning/reverting.
- boto3 underlying changelog: keep an eye on retries and chunked-encoding bugs.
- torch.load behavior: when loading map_location='cpu' it does streaming/unpickling; corrupt files raise UnpicklingError or EOFError.

Observed correlation with autoscaler events:
- Failures spike during scaling events where many instances pull same model concurrently. Could be S3 throttle / gateway limits -> truncated responses. Should consider staggering downloads or using signed URL distribution via CDN.

Immediate next steps (TODO):
- [ ] Add download verification step into serving init (try to draft quick patch) - assigned to me (Jordan) this week.
- [ ] Add logging to capture content-length and first 64 bytes of each shard when load fails (temp debug log level).
- [ ] Open quick runbook for on-call: how to detect corrupt shard and manual remediation (delete local cache, re-download, restart).
- [ ] Sync with training infra (owner: Miguel) to validate uploader atomicity and manifest behavior.

Things I want to capture for ticket INC-2345: exact timestamps of failures, gateway logs showing truncated response, and presigned URL sample that reproduced issue. Kept a copy of a truncated shard at /tmp/truncated-shard-sample.pt (28KB).

Slack threads and PRs to reference:
- #eng-serving-runtime thread: slack.redwood.com/archives/C01ABCDEF (see messages around Feb 24)
- Proposed quick fix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 (draft)

Misc small heuristics tried and results:
- Increasing boto3 retries to 8 reduced but did not eliminate failures.
- Switching from fsspec S3FileSystem to boto3 client.get_object stream gave slightly more consistent content-length reads on my test bench (yay), but not a long-term library swap decision yet.

If anyone picks this up: first check manifest in S3 for affected model, then try to reproduce by downloading shards using range requests and verifying header + checksum. Keep an eye on concurrent download rate from same prefix.

-- Jordan
(leave notes here before making PRs to keep context)
